Freeside · task page density · critique and counter-proposal · 4 Nov 2026

Task Page Density: What to Keep, What to Change

The 4 Nov proposal diagnoses the right problem: forensic facts draw at the same weight as the facts an operator reads. Its fix partly reverses an owner decision, rests on "as built" frames that don't match the app, and spends a plan §9 revision it doesn't need. The counter-proposal below gets more density with no plan change and no new mode: one forensic drawer per page (the existing Identifiers footer), the decision's inputs above its actions, the rest of the card foot gathered into Recorded Context, plus five fixes the proposal missed.

Revision 2 · after owner feedback
  1. The finding's reason is in the quote, clamped to two lines with an inline More that expands in place and is remembered per finding (§2). It's now part of the recommendation, not a variation.
  2. The Timeline is open by default. To make that work, the body splits into an always-open Current Run (with the live review rounds) and an open Timeline; only earlier attempts and campaigns fold, and the Task fold dissolves (§3).
  3. Prompt, Specification, and Pull Request get one quiet documents line under the status, each one click from its reader; a prompt-excerpt variation is drawn too (§3).
  4. Stage bands are gone. A plain "Show earlier events" cap stays as a measured fallback only.
Method
Every "Now" frame is a real render from main at df720455 (app/scripts/render-surfaces.sh, Mac, day, large text), not a redraw. The right-hand frames are mocks on the Overcast tokens and the Mac ladder, drawn at the same 1:1 scale, with the same fixture text where the render has it. Blue pins mark each change and are not UI.
What the proposal gets right
  1. Three altitudes (glance, read, forensic) is the right lens, and it maps onto pieces Freeside already has.
  2. Evidence above the actions. What an operator reads before deciding belongs above the act.
  3. Admission facts don't belong at reading weight in the Task fold, and the attempt card's Milestones list is the run page's job.
Where it goes wrong
  1. It re-adds a per-card technical fold the owner removed. On 21 Oct the owner called repeated technical disclosures "noisy and annoying" and chose one Identifiers footer per page (#2117). The proposal draws a Details fold on the card, inside the Task fold, and under History: three on one page, under the vaguest possible name, next to Run Details, which holds reading facts.
  2. Its "as built" frames are off. The real card foot has six folds and a quoted summary, not five folds, and none is named Details. The campaign fold is closed by default, so frame 4's count of 34 measures a state the operator sees only after opening it. Quote blocks aren't dashed (only the spec readers and follow-up text are), so frame 5's "each block keeps its dashed frame" isn't true.
  3. Frame 5 gets a consequence wrong. "You chose Fix in this PR instead; Accept All Dispositions keeps that choice" is false: Accept All sends the proposed routes, and only Choose Another Route sends a held pick. An operator who trusts that sentence loses their override.
  4. The plan §9 revision buys nothing. The word "(unverified)" isn't what makes those lines hard to read. The long producer phrase is. Shorten that phrase and keep the word.
  5. The ⌥⌘D switch is a mode. It's persistent per-device state stacked on per-task fold memory, it changes how values render, and it doubles the screenshot matrix, all for a debugging case that Copy all identifiers and hover-for-exact-time already cover.
What it missed (visible in the renders)
  1. Reading content sits under the forensic folds: the Agent Summary quote and Source and Original Report sit below Technical Bindings.
  2. Two More Actions menus on one page. The task's menu floats alone in the body.
  3. Every stage start repeats an event at the same timestamp: 3 of the 10 rail rows.
  4. The Task fold's summary repeats the eyebrow: 4 of 5 tokens.
  5. The forensic drawer holds reading facts: the reason, "Not available here: Convert to Policy", round counts. On finding adjudication, the Provenance fold splits the action group, and finding ids are in the reading path.

1 · The Seated Card: Inputs Above the Act, One Fold Below, Ids Join the Page

The rule that replaces the proposal's "one Details per card": if you'd copy it, it's in Identifiers; if you'd read it, it's in the body. A seated card adds its bindings to the page's one Identifiers footer as one more owner group, the shape #2117 already uses for the task, campaigns, and runs. Under its hairline the card keeps a single reading fold, the existing Recorded Context. Same fixture as the render: an agent question on #654.

2 · Finding Adjudication: Shorter Labels, the Reason in Reach

The proposal fixes a parsing problem with a plan §9 revision. The problem is a sentence-long producer keyword ("Model judgment with engine-authorized remediation"), not the word "(unverified)". Freeside already has the pattern that fixes it: the question card puts its keyword inside the quote and a compact mark trailing it ("Agent recommends", R21). Use that here, and every label keeps its word. No plan change, no decision note for §9.

Decline the finding

The path the reviewer cites is the client's resend, which already keeps the identity. 3 · The Body: The Timeline Open, the Current Run Open, the Documents One Click Away

Today every fold on the task page starts closed, including the current campaign, so the live review round sits two clicks down. Opening the Timeline by default only works if the page stops nesting the present inside the past. So the body splits by tense: Current Run (what's happening, always open), then Timeline (what happened, always open, newest first). Only the past folds: earlier attempts and earlier campaigns. The Task fold dissolves, because every row it held now has a better home, and the task's documents (prompt, specification, pull request) get one quiet line under the status.

4 · The Debugging Case: ⌥-Click, Not a Mode

The proposal adds View ▸ Show Technical Detail ⌥⌘D: a per-device switch that opens every fold and swaps short values for full digests and ISO instants, then hands back to "the per-device state they had". That's two layers of fold state, a rendering mode the screenshot matrix has to cover twice, and a control most operators never need. The debugging case already has Copy all identifiers (the whole set, grouped, as text) and exactInstant on every short time.

Recommended
  1. ⌥-click on any fold's chevron opens or closes it and every fold inside it, the macOS outline-view convention. ⌥-click an earlier campaign and you get its attempts, Round Facts, and Run Details; ⌥-click a finding's More and every reason on the card opens. ⌥-click Identifiers and you get every group. It writes the same per-fold memory a plain click does. No new state, no new control.
  2. No exact-value mode. Identifiers already shows full values, and hover (iPhone: long-press) already gives the exact instant.
  3. iPhone: nothing. Debugging happens on the Mac. On the phone, Copy all identifiers covers it.
If the owner still wants a menu item
Make it a one-shot command, View ▸ Expand All Folds, that opens every fold on the page and writes per-fold memory like a click would, so Collapse All Folds undoes it. It's a command, not a checked mode, and it never changes how a value renders.

7 · Owner Decisions, Order of Work, and What I Didn't Verify

Decisions (◆), each with a recommended answer
  1. ◆ A Does a seated card's bindings move into the page's Identifiers footer? Recommend yes. It extends #2117 to the last surface it didn't reach, and the card eyebrow's copy menu keeps single ids one gesture away.
  2. ◆ B Do task actions take the outline row's trailing slot (30 Oct ◆5)? Recommend yes, as "Task Actions ▾", and the navigation bar's trailing slot on iPhone. It ends the two-More Actions page and keeps Stop reachable while scrolled.
  3. ◆ C Do the Timeline and the current run start open, as sections rather than folds? Recommend yes. It reverses "every task-page fold starts closed" for exactly these two, and it dissolves the Task fold the 30 Oct note built from the inspector (every row moves, none is dropped). Earlier attempts and campaigns keep folding, with memory per id as today.
  4. ◆ D Does the task page get a documents line (Prompt, Specification, Pull Request)? Recommend yes, links only, with the prompt excerpt held back unless operators keep opening it. A work-item prompt likely needs a daemon read, so that half is a kind:contract unit; issue-sourced tasks and the PR can ship without one.
Order of work
  1. Card foot regroup and Identifiers join (§1), with Provenance moved above the actions and the id line dropped (§2). Client only, no rule change.
  2. Body: outline trailing menu, Conversation absent at zero, Current Run section and open Timeline with merged stage starts, Task fold dissolved, Milestones off the task page (§3).
  3. Finding labels and reasons: fixed keyword plus compact mark, and the clamped reason with More (§2). The labels are a wording change under plan §9's existing rule, so no revision.
  4. Documents line: Specification and Pull Request first (data the client may already reach), then Prompt after the daemon read lands (§3).
  5. ⌥-click recursive open (§4).
Each lands with a screenshot rebaseline. Item 1 changes where Technical Bindings lives, so publish_blocked's inspect scroll target moves with it.
Not verified
  • Whether the client holds per-finding confidence for every producer. If it doesn't, the mark falls back to "Agent".
  • That ⌥-click on a SwiftUI DisclosureGroup can be intercepted cleanly on macOS; SentenceDisclosure is custom, so it probably can.
  • The mocks' heights. They're estimates against the renders, not app measurements.
  • The data behind the proposal's richer rail rows ("on this Mac", "both fixed").
  • How the client gets the prompt and spec text. Task.source carries only a work-item artifact id or an issue ref, and the API has no read by artifact id. Timeline events carry approved_spec_digest, and GET /attachments/{digest} may serve those bytes, but I haven't confirmed the daemon allows that read for a spec digest.
  • Per-round outcome counts on the task page. RunReviewRound has an outcome; I haven't checked that finding counts are on the task timeline rather than only in the run read.
